status_note: known upstream: [duckdb-python#568](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-python/issues/568) (UHUGEINT >= 2^127 negative), open, untriaged; the lossy decimal mapping is deliberate ([duckdb-python#104](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-python/issues/104)). The HUGEINT >= 10^38 half has no issue. Reproduces on 2.0.0 and the 2.0.1/2.1.0 nightlies; `arrow_converter.cpp` unchanged on main (02aa9fa).
summary: DuckDB exports `HUGEINT` and `UHUGEINT` to Arrow as `decimal128(38, 0)` without a range check. A `UHUGEINT` of 2^127 or more arrives as a negative decimal (the maximum as -1), and positive values of 10^38 or more are decimals Arrow's validation rejects (pyarrow 26.0.1 accepts -2^127). Nothing raises.
repro:
```python
import duckdb
duckdb.sql("SELECT '340282366920938463463374607431768211455'::UHUGEINT AS u, '170141183460469231731687303715884105727'::HUGEINT AS h").to_arrow_table().to_pylist()
```
observed: `[{'u': Decimal('-1'), 'h': Decimal('170141183460469231731687303715884105727')}]`, and `validate(full=True)` of `h` raises "Decimal value … does not fit in precision of decimal128(38, 0)".
handling: sverify has no 128-bit integers. The replay harness (`sverify_dev.slt`) mirrors a `HUGEINT` or `UHUGEINT` column through Arrow only when all its values are below 10^38 in magnitude, which export exactly, and refuses the table otherwise, or when the column is nested (#618)
found_by: the characterization pipeline's round 3 (DuckDB's `uhugeint_try_cast.test` L115 replayed through `sverify_dev.slt`)
